claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or anything like that. He's actually started an apprenticeship though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

Is Alex's apprenticeship in England?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's not in England. He's doing his apprenticeship in Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Are there any other children you're inquiring about for Child Benefit, or is it just Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And it's just Alex I'm asking about, he's my only one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me confirm one final detail to complete my assessment:

Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and/or are you contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, accommodation, pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me at home, so I'm responsible for everything - his food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's the situation: The UK government rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts an apprenticeship **in England**. However, Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland, and the rules I have access to don't explicitly address whether apprenticeships in Northern Ireland (or other parts of the UK outside England) have the same effect on Child Benefit eligibility.

**What you should do:**

I recommend that you contact the Child Benefit Office directly to clarify how Alex's apprenticeship in Northern Ireland affects your eligibility. They will be able to provide you with definitive guidance on your specific circumstances.

You can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office by:
- Phone or post (details available on the gov.uk website)
- Through your online Child Benefit account if you have one

They'll be able to tell you whether you can continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex while he's doing his apprenticeship in Northern Ireland.
